title: Yogarāja Upaniṣad
subject: yoga
about: 21 mantras: the four yogas (mantra, laya, rāja, haṭha), their four common limbs, and meditation on nine cakras. The text follows Pt. Śrīrām Śarmā Ācārya's 108 Upaniṣads (Sādhanā-khaṇḍa); parts of mantras 9, 11 and 18 were unreadable in the scan and are given in the commonly printed reading.

lines.sa:
योगराजं प्रवक्ष्यामि योगिनां योगसिद्धये ।
मन्त्रयोगो लयश्चैव राजयोगो हठस्तथा ॥
lines.en: I shall teach the king of yogas, for the success of yogins: mantra yoga, laya, rāja yoga and haṭha.

lines.sa:
योगश्चतुर्विधः प्रोक्तो योगिभिस्तत्त्वदर्शिभिः ।
आसनं प्राणसंरोधो ध्यानं चैव समाधिकः ॥
lines.en: Yogins who see the truth call yoga fourfold. Posture, restraint of breath, meditation and samādhi —

lines.sa:
एतच्चतुष्टयं विद्धि सर्वयोगेषु सम्मतम् ।
ब्रह्मविष्णुशिवादीनां मन्त्रं जाप्यं विशारदैः ॥
lines.en: know these four to be accepted in every yoga. The wise repeat the mantras of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva and the other gods.

lines.sa:
साध्यते मन्त्रयोगस्तु वत्सराजादिभिर्यथा ।
कृष्णद्वैपायनाद्यैस्तु साधितो लयसंज्ञितः ॥
lines.en: Mantra yoga was accomplished by Vatsarāja and others; the yoga called laya by Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana (Vyāsa) and others,

lines.sa:
नवस्वेव हि चक्रेषु लयं कृत्वा महात्मभिः ।
प्रथमं ब्रह्मचक्रं स्यात् त्रिरावृत्तं भगाकृति ॥
lines.en: the great ones dissolving the mind in the nine cakras. The first is the brahma-cakra, coiled three times, triangular in shape.

lines.sa:
अपाने मूलकन्दाख्यं कामरूपं च तज्जगुः ।
तदेव वह्निकुण्डं स्यात् तत्त्वकुण्डलिनी तथा ॥
lines.en: At the place of apāna is what is called the root-bulb (mūlakanda), also named Kāmarūpa; it is the pit of fire, and there is the kuṇḍalinī.

lines.sa:
तां जीवरूपिणीं ध्यायेज्ज्योतिष्ठं मुक्तिहेतवे ।
स्वाधिष्ठानं द्वितीयं स्याच्चक्रं तन्मध्यगं विदुः ॥
lines.en: Meditate on her, who is of the form of the living self and of light, for the sake of liberation. The second cakra is svādhiṣṭhāna; within it,

lines.sa:
पश्चिमाभिमुखं लिङ्गं प्रवालाङ्कुरसन्निभम् ।
तत्रोड्डीयाणपीठेषु तं ध्यात्वाकर्षयेज्जगत् ॥
lines.en: a liṅga facing west, like a shoot of coral. Meditating on it there in the Uḍḍīyāṇa seat, one draws the world to oneself.

lines.sa:
तृतीयं नाभिचक्रं स्यात्तन्मध्ये तु जगत् स्थितम् ।
पञ्चावर्तां मध्यशक्तिं चिन्तयेद्विद्युदाकृतिम् ॥
lines.en: The third is the navel cakra; the world rests within it. Think there of the power in its middle, with five coils, like lightning.

lines.sa:
तां ध्यात्वा सर्वसिद्धीनां भाजनं जायते बुधः ।
चतुर्थे हृदये चक्रे विज्ञेयं तदधोमुखम् ॥
lines.en: Meditating on her, the wise one becomes a vessel of all siddhis. The fourth, the heart cakra, is to be known as facing downward.

lines.sa:
ज्योतीरूपं च तन्मध्ये हंसं ध्यायेत् प्रयत्नतः ।
तं ध्यायतो जगत् सर्वं वश्यं स्यान्नात्र संशयः ॥
lines.en: In its middle meditate with effort on the haṃsa in the form of light; for one who does, the whole world comes under control — of this there is no doubt.

lines.sa:
पञ्चमं कण्ठचक्रं स्यात् तत्र वामे इडा भवेत् ।
दक्षिणे पिङ्गला ज्ञेया सुषुम्ना मध्यतः स्थिता ॥
lines.en: The fifth is the throat cakra: iḍā is on its left, piṅgalā on the right, and suṣumnā in the middle.

lines.sa:
तत्र ध्यात्वा शुचि ज्योतिः सिद्धीनां भाजनं भवेत् ।
षष्ठं च तालुकाचक्रं घण्टिकास्थानमुच्यते ॥
lines.en: Meditating there on the pure light, one becomes a vessel of siddhis. The sixth is the palate cakra, called the place of the uvula (ghaṇṭikā).

lines.sa:
दशमद्वारमार्गं तद्राजदन्तं च तज्जगुः ।
तत्र शून्ये लयं कृत्वा मुक्तो भवति निश्चितम् ॥
lines.en: It is the way to the tenth door, and is also called the 'royal tooth'. Dissolving the mind in the void there, one is surely freed.

lines.sa:
भ्रूचक्रं सप्तमं विद्याद्बिन्दुस्थानं च तद्विदुः ।
भ्रुवोर्मध्ये वर्तुलं च ध्यात्वा ज्योतिः प्रमुच्यते ॥
lines.en: Know the seventh as the brow cakra, the seat of the bindu. Meditating on the round light between the eyebrows, one is freed.

lines.sa:
अष्टमं ब्रह्मरन्ध्रं स्यात् परं निर्वाणसूचकम् ।
तं ध्यात्वा सूतिकाग्रामं धूमाकारं विमुच्यते ॥
lines.en: The eighth is the brahmarandhra, which points to the highest nirvāṇa. Meditating on it, smoke-coloured, one is freed. (Other editions read sūcikāgrābham, 'fine as the point of a needle'.)

lines.sa:
तच्च जालन्धरं ज्ञेयं मोक्षदं नीलचेतसम् ।
नवमं व्योमचक्रं स्यादश्रैः षोडशभिर्युतम् ॥
lines.en: It is to be known as Jālandhara, the giver of liberation. The ninth is the space cakra (vyoma-cakra), with sixteen petals.

lines.sa:
संविद्ब्रूयाच्च तन्मध्ये शक्तिरुद्धा स्थिता परा ।
तत्र पूर्णां गिरौ पीठे शक्तिं ध्यात्वा विमुच्यते ॥
lines.en: In its middle stands the supreme power, called saṃvid (consciousness). Meditating there on the full power in the Pūrṇagiri seat, one is freed.

lines.sa:
एतेषां नवचक्राणामेकैकं ध्यायतो मुनेः ।
सिद्धयो मुक्तिसहिताः करस्थाः स्युर्दिने दिने ॥
lines.en: For the sage who meditates on these nine cakras one by one, the siddhis, together with liberation, come into his hand day by day.

lines.sa:
एको दण्डद्वयं मध्ये पश्यति ज्ञानचक्षुषा ।
कदम्बगोलकाकारं ब्रह्मलोकं व्रजन्ति ते ॥
lines.en: Those who see with the eye of knowledge the two staffs in the middle of the sphere shaped like a kadamba ball go to the world of Brahmā.

lines.sa:
ऊर्ध्वशक्तिनिपातेन अधःशक्तेर्निकुञ्चनात् ।
मध्यशक्तिप्रबोधेन जायते परमं सुखं जायते परमं सुखम् ॥
lines.en: By bringing down the upper power, by contracting the lower power and by awakening the middle power, the highest bliss arises.
